rows.question: why is my circuit not getting any gain
rows.answer:
Your circuit has no gain because there is no signal path at all - the input is not connected to the network.

What the netlist actually says:

  V1 Vin 0 AC 0.7 3000
  R1 Vout NC_01 10k     <- left pin dangling
  R2 Vout 0 15k
  C1 Vout 0 6.63n
  .ac dec 10 1k 100k

Net 'Vin' has exactly one connection (V1 only) and R1's other pin sits on the auto-named node NC_01, which is LTspice's way of saying "no wire touches this pin." So the source drives nothing, and Vout is tied only to R2 and C1, both of which go to ground. V(Vout) is therefore identically 0 at every frequency - a flat -inf dB curve, i.e. "no gain."

Fix: wire the free (left) end of R1 to the Vin node / the top of V1. This is a rewiring, not a value change, so it has to be done in the schematic - drag a wire from R1's dangling pin to the V1 output node. After that the netlist line should read:

  R1 Vin Vout 10k

Two things to expect once it's connected, since you said "gain":

1. This is a passive RC low-pass with a resistive divider, so it can only attenuate. DC/low-frequency gain = R2/(R1+R2) = 15k/25k = 0.6 (-4.4 dB). With Vin = 0.7 V AC that is 0.42 V out. If you wanted unity passband gain you need an active stage or R1 replaced by a series element that isn't part of a divider.

2. The corner is set by C1 against the parallel combination seen from Vout: R1||R2 = 10k*15k/25k = 6.0k.
   f_c = 1/(2*pi*6000*6.63n) = 1/(2*pi*3.978e-5) = 4.00 kHz.
   Your .ac sweep runs 1k to 100k, so you will see the 0.6 plateau up to ~4 kHz and then -20 dB/decade. If you intended a different cutoff, tell me the target and I'll give you the C1 value.

Also note the '3000' in V1's value is being read as the AC phase (AC <mag> <phase>), not a frequency - the sweep frequencies come from .ac. If you meant something else there, drop it and just use 'AC 0.7'.
